advisor_identified: John Tupper (Jack) Saywell, historian of Canadian politics and constitutional history at York University and former director of its Graduate Program in History.

doctorate.title: The Office of the Lieutenant Governor: A Study in Canadian Government and Politics

evidence.says: School Administration for a Humanistic Era (1973), printed p. 32, identifies John Saywell as York University's Dean of the Faculty of Arts and lists his PhD as Harvard, 1956.

Identifies John Tupper Saywell as a political historian with a Harvard PhD, York's founding dean of Arts and Science, and director of its Graduate Program in History from 1987 to 1998. Lists his 1957 book The Office of Lieutenant-Governor: A Study in Canadian Government and Politics and its Harvard Delancey K. Jay Prize.

The Canadian Historical Association's 1976 bulletin identifies John Tupper Saywell as a York professor and states that he completed his Harvard doctorate in 1956 (search-indexed text; direct PDF retrieval failed).

notes: The Harvard institution and 1956 year independently match AHA record 51608. The dissertation title is retained from the supplied AHA record; no independent thesis catalogue record was located. His documented 1957 book has essentially the same title, supporting the identification.
